# -replay reads a recording instead of NVML, so it needs no GPU.
# -s prints the first frame; -l prints every frame.
exec nvtop -x -replay rec.jsonl -s
stdout '^   "device_name": "NVIDIA GB10",$'
stdout '^   "gpu_util": "3%",$'
! stdout '"gpu_util": "41%"'
! stderr .

exec nvtop -x -replay rec.jsonl -l
stdout '"gpu_util": "3%"'
stdout '"gpu_util": "41%"'
stdout '"cmdline": "python train.py"'
! stderr .

# The extension flags need -x.
! exec nvtop -replay rec.jsonl -s
stderr '^nvtop: -replay needs -x$'

! exec nvtop -x -replay missing.jsonl -s
stderr '^nvtop: open missing.jsonl: '

! exec nvtop -x -replay bad.jsonl -s
stderr '^nvtop: replay bad.jsonl: '
